messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: "az-west-2 - inference-pool CPU & eviction surge". Incident: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD123456. Summary: sustained pod evictions and autoscaler thrash in az-west-2 affecting Redwood-hosted inference pools. Estimated impact: increased 5xx and p99 latency for some customers, potential failover recommended. Tags: #az-west-2 #evictions #autoscaler

pagerduty-bot: Incident PD123456 assigned to sara (oncall). Priority: P1. Escalation policy: oncall-sre.

sara (oncall): Ack. Looking now. Starting investigation — pulling metrics and node events. @ana please stand by for possible handoff.

mike (prod-eng): Noted. Any sign it's a regional infra issue (hosts failing) vs. workload spike?

sara (oncall): Early signals: eviction rate jumped ~x25 over baseline, kubelet OOM/kicked pods. 5xx rate on public-api route jumped from 0.2% -> ~11% in last 3m. P99 generation latency up from 480ms -> 6.8s.

ana (sre): joining. Can you paste node event stream and autoscaler logs?

sara (oncall): paste: ```
$ kubectl get pods -n redwood-inference -o wide | grep az-west-2
inference-ttq-1    CrashLoopBackOff   3/5   10m    10.0.2.45   az-west-2a
inference-ttq-2    Running            5/5   12m    10.0.2.46   az-west-2b
worker-abc          Evicted            0/1   2m     <none>     az-west-2c
```
Recent node events: `kubelet_eviction_threshold exceeded`, `kernel: oom_reaper invoked on process`. Autoscaler log excerpt: `scale-down: suppressed due to pending evictions; scale-up failed: Insufficient capacity in AZ`.

jess (support): Support sees ~12 distinct customer sessions with errors right now, mainly enterprise routes behind dedicated pools. Logged tickets from two customers reporting 503s.

mike (prod-eng): If autoscaler failing due to zone capacity, we should flip traffic away from az-west-2 for the affected routes. Can we trigger the regional fallback/routing policy?

sara (oncall): Agree. Recommend initiating controlled fallback: shift 40% of affected traffic to az-east-1, enable degraded-mode for heavy models, keep eviction-prone instances out of rotation. Will coordinate.

mike (prod-eng): Initiating routing fallback for model-group 'redwood-gen-large' using redwoodctl. Command: ```
# flip 40% of routed traffic from az-west-2 -> az-east-1 for affected route
redwoodctl route update --route-id r-9876 --weight az-west-2=60,az-east-1=40 --reason "auto-fallback - az-west-2 capacity"
```

deploy-bot: Routing change job started: job/route-update-2149001128. Watch logs at https://console.redwood/jobs/job-2149001128

ana (sre): While that runs, I'll try to provision burst instances in az-west-2 (if capacity permits) and also adjust kube eviction thresholds to avoid immediate churn. If provisioning fails, we'll keep fallback active.

sara (oncall): Running quick health checks on ded pools: ```
$ redwoodctl pool ls --region az-west-2
pool:d-42 status: degraded active: 12 desired: 20 evictions: 8
pool:d-43 status: healthy active: 24 desired: 24 evictions: 0
```

jess (support): Notifying affected customers now with initial message: "We're investigating increased errors in az-west-2; routing mitigations underway; we'll update within 30 minutes."

pagerduty-bot: PD PD123456: ack by sara (oncall) at 2149001120. No unacked escalations pending.

sara (oncall): Route update confirmed by job logs. Traffic shift at 2149001135. Monitoring error rate.

mike (prod-eng): I'm also adding temporary node pool with smaller instances to absorb warmups: `cloudctl create-instances --region az-west-2 --type g4dn.xlarge --count 8 --tag temp-fallback`.

ana (sre): Manual scale-up attempt returned partial success: 5 nodes provisioned, 3 pending due to resource limits. Adjusted kube eviction soft limit to 85% memory; this should reduce churn.

sara (oncall): Metrics update: 5xx dropped from 11% -> 3.2% after traffic shift and eviction threshold change. P99 down to 1.2s for most routes. Still seeing some errors for heavy long-seq jobs.

jess (support): Customers updated: two enterprise customers asked for ETA on full recovery; told them monitoring in 15m windows, will escalate if not back to normal.

mike (prod-eng): I've also opened a cloud capacity request with provider; ETA unknown. Recommend keeping fallback config for 2 hours and gradually move back once nodes stable.

sara (oncall): Agreed. I'll keep PD incident open and mark mitigation in timeline. If no regression in 30m, we'll start rolling traffic back to az-west-2.

deploy-bot: Routing job job/route-update-2149001128 completed successfully at 2149001136.

incident-bot: Incident PD123456 timeline note: 2149001120 ack, 2149001135 traffic shift initiated, 2149001142 autoscaler scale-up partial, 2149001202 error-rate improvement observed.

ana (sre): Quick post-mortem notes to capture: root cause likely a combination of provider-side capacity pressure in az-west-2 plus an autoscaler suppression condition that prevented sufficient warm-up capacity. Need follow-ups: adjust autoscaler backoff, add provider fallback quota, refine eviction thresholds.

sara (oncall): PD incident remains open for follow-ups. Current state: mitigation active, customer impact reduced to degraded performance for a small subset. Monitoring for 30m.

jess (support): Sending final interim update to affected customers: "Traffic rerouted and mitigations in place; majority of requests restored; next update in 30 minutes." :thumbsup:

mike (prod-eng): Thanks team. If all stays green, I'll coordinate a revert runbook later to bring traffic back to az-west-2 and terminate temp nodes.

incident-bot: PD123456: resolved by sara (oncall) at 2149001355. Resolution note: routing fallback + eviction threshold change + partial scale-up mitigated symptoms; provider capacity issue reported to vendor for follow-up.

sara (oncall): Closing thread here. Will file follow-up issue with action items and assign owners. Monitoring window starts now (30m). Thanks everyone.
